This chain of interactions implies a potential mechanism by which Kojic acid influences macrophage function, possibly through autophagy-related pathways. The integration of these relationships highlights a possible role for Kojic acid in modulating macrophage-expressed gene 1 protein expression, though the exact functional significance remains to be elucidated. The evidence supports a pathway where Kojic acid indirectly affects macrophage gene expression via its interaction with Beclin-1 and 1,2-dihydroxybenzene, suggesting a broader role in cellular regulation.
